A critical point of $f(x)$ is a point $x=c$ in the domain of $f$ such that either ${f}^{′}(c)=0$ or ${f}^{′}(c)$ does not exist.

Differentiating $f(x),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡x+7\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡x+7\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

We now proceed to find the critical points:

- First, we compute the points where ${f}^{′}(c)=0.$ We set the derivative equal to zero, and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-2\operatorname{sin}⁡x+7\operatorname{cos}⁡x & =0 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡x & =\frac{7}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} & =\frac{7}{2}\cdot \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡x & =\frac{7}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{7}{2})+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $-\pi <x<\pi .$

- setting $n=0$ gives $x≈1.292\,50$ rounded to five decimal places

- setting $n=-1$ gives $x≈-1.849\,10$ rounded to five decimal places

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $-\pi <x<\pi .$ So, the solutions to this equation for $x\in (-\pi ,\pi )$ are 

$$
x≈1.292\,50,\,x≈-1.849\,10.
$$

Therefore, $f(x)$ has stationary points at $x≈-1.849\,10$ and $x≈1.292\,50.$

- Second, we note that ${f}^{′}(x)$ exists for all values of $x\in (-\pi ,\pi ).$ So $f(x)$ has no non-stationary critical points.

Therefore, we conclude that the critical points of $f(x)$ for $x\in (-\pi ,\pi )$ are ${x}_{1}≈-1.849\,10$ and ${x}_{2}≈1.292\,50.$

Finally,

$$
{x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}≈-1.849\,10\cdot 1.292\,50≈-2.39
$$

rounded to two decimal places
